legend: The contest arena is under attack ! George wants to save it, so he will use his special ability called "One Punch MEX".
George has n$$$n$$$ power stones numbered from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$. For n$$$n$$$ times the following action will happen in order:
Uniformly at random, one of the stones will disappear
The MEX of the remaining stones will add to the One Punch MEX damage
George is wondering what will be the expected damage of the One Punch MEX if he has n$$$n$$$ power stones
MEX is the minimum positive number not present in the set. MEX of []$$$[]$$$ is 1$$$1$$$, MEX of [3,5,1]$$$[3,5,1]$$$ is 2$$$2$$$
input: The first line contains the number of test cases t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤105)$$$( 1 \le t \le 10^{5} )$$$. A description of the test cases follows
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤105)$$$( 1 \le n \le 10^{5} )$$$ indicating the number of power stones
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 105$$$10^{5}$$$
output: For each test case, output a single line containing the expected damage of One Punch MEX modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$
note: With the probability 12$$$\frac{1}{2}$$$, the first stone will be removed, then the second stone with the sum of MEX equal to 2
With the probability 12$$$\frac{1}{2}$$$, the second stone will be removed, then the first stone with the sum of MEX equal to 3
The expected damage of One Punch MEX is 52$$$\frac{5}{2}$$$
